LDSO-Epistemic: Claims, Sources, Trust and Conflict Resolution

Abstract

LDSO-Epistemic is an RDF/OWL vocabulary for what sources claim, as opposed to what is true: claims (one asserted triple, possibly denied) with a source, a confidence and a time; corrections and retractions; the trust a source carries; the resolution policy that settles conflicts between claims; and the stored result of an assessment (accepted, rejected, contested, undetermined or not admitted), with the decisions that explain it. It compiles to the hydradl-epistemic engine and builds on [[LDSO-CORE]].

Status notice: This document is not an official W3C Standard or W3C Recommendation. It is a community/project specification using W3C ReSpec formatting conventions.

This document is not an official W3C Standard or W3C Recommendation. It is a community/project specification using W3C ReSpec formatting conventions.

This is draft 0.1.0, produced by Geoknoesis LLC. Ontology IRI: https://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic — version IRI https://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic/0.1.0 — preferred prefix epi:. Feedback is welcome via the GitHub issue tracker.

Overview

LDSO-Epistemic is the vocabulary for what sources claim, as opposed to what is true: claims (one asserted triple, possibly denied) with a source, a confidence and a time; corrections (epi:supersedes) and retractions; the trust a source carries (a tier, an admission floor); the policy that settles conflicts between claims (an ordered list of criteria, optionally per property or class); and the result of an assessment (a status per claim, the conflicts found, the decisions taken).

It reuses PROV-O (a claim is a prov:Entity, epi:claimedBy is a sub-property of prov:wasAttributedTo) and is designed so that claims, sources and a policy map to the belief-revision engine of HydraDL (hydradl-epistemic). The engine decides, against a trusted OWL 2 DL ontology, which claims to accept, reject or leave contested, and explains each status.

Layer Module Says
2b LDSO-Entities / LDSO-Annotations (ent:, ann:) what a text mentions, with the score of the extractor
6 LDSO-Epistemic (epi:) who claims what, how far each source is trusted, and which claims survive when they conflict

A claim derived from an ann:EntityMention uses prov:wasDerivedFrom that mention and copies its confidence when the mention states one. A mention with no score gives a claim with no epi:confidence (not stated), not 1.0.

Properties

Property Domain → Range Notes
epi:negated Claim → xsd:boolean the claim denies its triple; absent: false
epi:claimedBy Claim or Retraction → Source sub-property of prov:wasAttributedTo; pointing at a claim is nested attribution (gap E1)
epi:confidence Claim → xsd:decimal [0,1] absent means not stated; skos:closeMatch ann:confidence
epi:claimedAt Claim or Retraction → xsd:dateTime skos:closeMatch prov:generatedAtTime
epi:supersedes Claim → Claim correction
epi:retracts Retraction → Claim withdrawal
epi:tier Source → xsd:nonNegativeInteger higher is more trusted
epi:admissionFloor Source or Policy → xsd:decimal [0,1]
epi:criteria Policy or ScopedChain → rdf:List of Criterion ordered
epi:appliesTo ScopedChain → property or class IRI
epi:confidenceMargin Policy → xsd:decimal [0,1]
epi:hasScopedChain Policy → ScopedChain
epi:assesses Assessment → Claim
epi:status Assessment → ClaimStatus
epi:reason Assessment → xsd:string
epi:involves Conflict → Claim
epi:compares Decision → Claim exactly two per decision: the claims compared, decided or not
epi:winner, epi:loser Decision → Claim only when a criterion decided; sub-properties of epi:compares
epi:decidedBy Decision → Criterion only when a criterion decided
epi:comparedValues Decision → xsd:string
epi:corroborates Claim → Claim gap E2
epi:validFrom, epi:validUntil Claim → xsd:dateTime gap E3
epi:trustedFor Source → any gap E5
epi:trustLevel Source → skos:Concept gap E6

Dates

epi:claimedAt (and the gap properties epi:validFrom / epi:validUntil) take xsd:dateTime, in UTC, for example "2026-03-04T00:00:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime. hydradl-dl supports xsd:dateTime, not xsd:date: a claimed date written as xsd:date is not read as an instant. The engine keeps whole seconds since the Unix epoch.

Confidence and ann:confidence

epi:confidence is not declared equivalent to ann:confidence. LDSO-Annotations reads an absent score as 1.0 (a human-curated annotation); the epistemic layer reads it as not stated: such a claim is never below an admission floor and never decides a comparison by confidence. The two are related by skos:closeMatch only. RDF 1.2 triple terms are noted as a skos:relatedMatch of epi:Claim.

RDF → Rust mapping

There is no compiler yet: the table is the contract for the one a builder will write. Rust names are those of crates/hydradl-epistemic/src; Query, Name and Ontology come from hydradl-dl.

RDF Rust
epi:Source + epi:tier / epi:admissionFloor Source { id, tier: Option<u32>, floor: Option<Confidence> }
epi:Claim Claim { id, assertion: Query, source, confidence, at, supersedes }
rdf:subject / rdf:predicate / rdf:object of a claim Claim::assertion, a Query (rules below)
predicate rdf:type Query::ClassAssertion(individual, class)
predicate rdf:type with epi:negated true Query::ClassAssertion(individual, Class::Not(class))
predicate any other, object an IRI Query::ObjectPropertyAssertion(subject, role, object)
predicate any other, object a literal Query::DataPropertyAssertion(subject, property, literal)
epi:negated true on a property assertion Query::NegativeObjectPropertyAssertion / Query::NegativeDataPropertyAssertion
predicate owl:sameAs (not negated) or owl:differentFrom with epi:negated true Query::SameIndividual(a, b)
predicate owl:differentFrom (not negated) or owl:sameAs with epi:negated true Query::DifferentIndividuals(a, b)
epi:claimedBy Claim::source / Retraction::source (a Name naming a Source)
epi:confidence Claim::confidence: Option<Confidence> (millionths in a u32, 0..=1_000_000)
epi:claimedAt Claim::at / Retraction::at: Option<i64>, seconds, UTC
epi:supersedes Claim::supersedes: Vec<Name>
epi:Retraction + epi:retracts Retraction { id, source, at, retracts: Vec<Name> }
epi:ResolutionPolicy Policy { floor, margin, chain, overrides, max_calls, max_repairs }
policy epi:admissionFloor Policy::floor
epi:confidenceMargin Policy::margin (default 0.05)
policy epi:criteria Policy::chain: Vec<Criterion> (default tier, confidence, recency)
epi:ByTier / epi:ByConfidence / epi:ByRecency Criterion::Tier / Criterion::Confidence / Criterion::Recency
epi:ScopedChain + epi:appliesTo + epi:criteria one entry of Policy::overrides: Vec<(Scope, Vec<Criterion>)>
epi:appliesTo a property IRI Scope::Property(name)
epi:appliesTo a class IRI Scope::Class(name)
epi:Assessment Assessment { claim, status, reason }
epi:status ClaimStatus::{Accepted, Rejected, Contested, Undetermined, NotAdmitted}
epi:reason Reason::{NoConflict, Retracted, BelowFloor, Superseded, Conflicts, Undetermined}, rendered by Display
epi:Conflict + epi:involves Conflict { id, claims, decisions }
epi:Decision + epi:compares / epi:winner / epi:loser / epi:decidedBy / epi:comparedValues Decision { winner, loser, by: DecidedBy, chain: ChainUsed }, rendered by Display: epi:compares is the pair {winner, loser}; epi:winner, epi:loser and epi:decidedBy are written only when by is not DecidedBy::Undecided

A denied rdf:type claim is the assertion of the complement class. It is not looked up under the class's scoped chain: an epi:ScopedChain that epi:appliesTo a class applies to claims asserting that named class, so a claim denying it is compared by the default chain.

A Belief collects the sources, claims, retractions and policy over a trusted Ontology; Belief::validate() reports the errors below as EpistemicError.

Statuses and reasons

Five statuses, with the wording of the engine's Display:

Status Meaning Reason shown
epi:Accepted in every optimal repair no conflict, or in conflict N, M when the claim won every conflict
epi:Rejected in no optimal repair in conflict N, M
epi:Contested in some optimal repairs, not all in conflict N, M
epi:Undetermined the group could not be settled undetermined: <message>, for example more than 1024 optimal repairs or repair search exceeded 65536 repairs
epi:NotAdmitted left out before conflicts were considered retracted by R, confidence C below floor F or superseded by X

An assessment reads c_news: rejected (in conflict 0). A decision reads c_registry outranks c_news: tier 3 over tier 1 (tier 1 over no tier when the loser's source has no tier), ... confidence 0.91 over 0.8 (margin 0.05), ... claimed at A, after B, or a and b are undecided after tier, confidence, recency, followed by [chain for P] when a scoped chain was used. A conflict of one claim reads conflict N: c contradicts the trusted ontology.

A stored epi:Decision always names its two claims with epi:compares. It names an epi:winner, an epi:loser and an epi:decidedBy, each once, only when a criterion decided the pair. An undecided pair has none of the three (the engine orders an undecided pair by id internally, but that order is no preference and is not written), and its epi:comparedValues reads undecided after tier, confidence, recency. shapes.ttl enforces this: exactly two epi:compares, the three properties all present or all absent, and the winner and the loser among the compared claims. A query for winners therefore needs no filter on epi:decidedBy, but a query over all compared pairs must use epi:compares, not epi:winner.

A claim failing several admission tests reports the first in this order: retracted, below the floor, superseded. A claim whose replacement was itself retracted or fell below the floor is not superseded.

Gaps

Valid LDSO-Epistemic that the engine does not run (reported by the profile shapes, hydradl-profile-shapes.ttl, and illustrated by examples/gaps.ttl): E1 nested attribution (epi:claimedBy pointing at a claim), E2 epi:corroborates, E3 epi:validFrom / epi:validUntil, E4 claims about the ontology (a claim whose triple is a TBox axiom), E5 epi:trustedFor, E6 epi:trustLevel or a tier whose type is not an integer (graded trust). One source rating another has no LDSO-Epistemic term and is outside the vocabulary for now.

Usage Pattern

ex:Ireland owl:differentFrom ex:Malta .   # in the trusted ontology

ex:src_registry a epi:Source ; epi:tier 3 .
ex:src_news     a epi:Source ; epi:tier 1 ; epi:admissionFloor 0.7 .

ex:c_registry a epi:Claim ;
  rdf:subject ex:acme ; rdf:predicate ex:registeredIn ; rdf:object ex:Ireland ;
  epi:claimedBy ex:src_registry ;
  epi:claimedAt "2026-03-04T00:00:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime .

ex:c_news a epi:Claim ;
  rdf:subject ex:acme ; rdf:predicate ex:registeredIn ; rdf:object ex:Malta ;
  epi:claimedBy ex:src_news ; epi:confidence 0.91 .

ex:policy a epi:ResolutionPolicy ;
  epi:criteria ( epi:ByTier epi:ByConfidence epi:ByRecency ) .

With ex:registeredIn functional in the trusted ontology, the two claims conflict, the registry's tier decides, and ex:c_registry is accepted while ex:c_news is rejected. The owl:differentFrom is needed: OWL makes no unique name assumption, so without it a functional ex:registeredIn only infers that ex:Ireland and ex:Malta are the same country, and the two claims do not conflict (examples/kyc.ttl states ex:UK owl:differentFrom ex:CY for the same reason).

The KYC example

examples/kyc.ttl is the executable example and the scenario of the Rust test crates/hydradl-epistemic/tests/kyc.rs: five sources (the registry and the sanctions list at tier 3, the onboarding form at tier 2, two news sources at tier 1) make 13 claims about the company ex:acme, with one retraction and one correction, under a policy with an admission floor of 0.5, a confidence margin of 0.05, the default chain tier, confidence, recency, and a scoped chain recency, tier for ex:registeredAddress. The engine finds four conflicts and gives these statuses (the stored result at the end of kyc.ttl):

Claim Says Status Why
ex:regDoi incorporated 2011-03-04 (registry) accepted conflict 2: tier 3 over tier 1
ex:nerDoi incorporated 2012-03-04 (news, 0.8) rejected conflict 2
ex:newsUk incorporated in the UK (news, 0.91) contested conflict 3: same tier, 0.91 against 0.88 is within the margin, no times
ex:newsCy incorporated in Cyprus (news, 0.88) contested conflict 3
ex:formAddrOld address "1 Old St" (form) not admitted superseded by ex:formAddrNew
ex:formAddrNew address "2 New St" (form, 2025) accepted conflict 0: claimed later, by the scoped chain
ex:regAddr address "9 Registry Rd" (registry, 2023) rejected conflict 0
ex:regActive an active company (registry) accepted no conflict
ex:newsDissolved a dissolved company (news, 0.7) not admitted retracted by ex:newsBRetract
ex:nerShell a shell company (news, 0.4) not admitted confidence 0.4 below floor 0.5
ex:sancIvan Ivan is a sanctioned person (sanctions list) accepted conflict 1: tier 3 over both
ex:formCleared Acme is cleared (form) accepted conflict 1: tier 2 over tier 1
ex:newsControl Acme is controlled by Ivan (news, 0.9) rejected conflict 1

Conflict 1 has three claims: control by a sanctioned person makes Acme sanctions-exposed, which is disjoint from cleared. The only optimal repair keeps the two higher-tier claims and drops the news item.

The stored decisions show both forms: ex:d_address and the three decisions of conflict 1 compare two claims and name the winner, the loser and the deciding criterion; ex:d_country, the decision of conflict 3, compares ex:newsCy and ex:newsUk and names no winner, loser or criterion (undecided after tier, confidence, recency).

Class Reference

epi:Assessment

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Assessment
LabelAssessment
Subclass ofprov:Entity
DefinitionThe outcome for one claim: its status and why.
UsageCorresponds to a HydraDL Assessment. Stored results are Layer 6 data; the engine returns them, it does not read them.
ex:a_news
  a epi:Assessment ;
  epi:assesses ex:c_news ;
  epi:status epi:Rejected ;
  epi:reason "in conflict 0" .

epi:Claim

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Claim
LabelClaim
Subclass ofrdf:Statement, prov:Entity
DefinitionOne triple asserted by a source, which may be denied (epi:negated), carried by rdf:subject, rdf:predicate and rdf:object.
UsageA claim is not a fact: the trusted ontology and other claims decide whether it is accepted. With rdf:type as predicate it is a class assertion; with owl:sameAs or owl:differentFrom it is an identity claim; with any other predicate it is an object property assertion when the object is an IRI and a data property assertion when it is a literal. A claim has exactly one subject, predicate and object, and one epi:claimedBy. RDF 1.2 triple terms are the closest standard counterpart (see alignments.ttl); a claim node is used so that confidence, source and time attach to it in RDF 1.1.
ex:c_registry
  a epi:Claim ;
  rdf:subject ex:acme ;
  rdf:predicate ex:registeredIn ;
  rdf:object ex:Ireland ;
  epi:claimedBy ex:src_registry ;
  epi:confidence 1.0 ;
  epi:claimedAt "2026-03-04T00:00:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime .

epi:ClaimStatus

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#ClaimStatus
LabelClaim Status
Subclass ofskos:Concept
DefinitionWhat an assessment concluded about a claim.
UsageFive individuals: epi:Accepted, epi:Rejected, epi:Contested, epi:Undetermined and epi:NotAdmitted.
epi:Accepted a epi:ClaimStatus .

epi:Conflict

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Conflict
LabelConflict
Subclass ofprov:Entity
DefinitionA minimal set of admitted claims that the trusted ontology cannot hold together. A conflict of one claim is a claim that contradicts the ontology on its own.
UsageCorresponds to a HydraDL Conflict. Claims are linked with epi:involves.
ex:conflict_0
  a epi:Conflict ;
  epi:involves ex:c_registry , ex:c_news .

epi:Criterion

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Criterion
LabelCriterion
Subclass ofskos:Concept
DefinitionA way to prefer one claim over another.
UsageThree individuals: epi:ByTier, epi:ByConfidence and epi:ByRecency.
epi:ByTier a epi:Criterion .

epi:Decision

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Decision
LabelDecision
Subclass ofprov:Entity
DefinitionHow two conflicting claims were compared: the two claims (epi:compares) and, when a criterion decided, which one won, which one lost, and by which criterion.
UsageCorresponds to a HydraDL Decision. Every decision has exactly two epi:compares values, the claims compared, decided or not. epi:winner, epi:loser and epi:decidedBy are present, each exactly once, only when a criterion of the chain decided the pair; the winner and the loser are then the two compared claims. When no criterion decides, the pair is undecided: the decision has none of the three, and its epi:comparedValues starts "undecided after" and lists the criteria tried. A decision prefers one claim only when it has an epi:decidedBy.
ex:d_0
  a epi:Decision ;
  epi:compares ex:c_registry , ex:c_news ;
  epi:winner ex:c_registry ;
  epi:loser ex:c_news ;
  epi:decidedBy epi:ByTier ;
  epi:comparedValues "tier 3 over tier 1" .

# Undecided: same tier, confidences within the margin, no claim time.
ex:d_1
  a epi:Decision ;
  epi:compares ex:c_uk , ex:c_cy ;
  epi:comparedValues "undecided after tier, confidence, recency" .

epi:ResolutionPolicy

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#ResolutionPolicy
LabelResolution Policy
Subclass ofprov:Entity
DefinitionHow conflicts between claims are settled: an admission floor, a confidence margin, a default chain of criteria and chains for particular properties or classes.
UsageCorresponds to a HydraDL Policy. The default chain is tier, then confidence, then recency when no epi:criteria is stated; the default margin is 0.05.
ex:policy
  a epi:ResolutionPolicy ;
  epi:admissionFloor 0.5 ;
  epi:confidenceMargin 0.05 ;
  epi:criteria ( epi:ByTier epi:ByConfidence epi:ByRecency ) ;
  epi:hasScopedChain ex:chain_address .

epi:Retraction

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Retraction
LabelRetraction
Subclass ofprov:Entity
DefinitionA source's withdrawal of earlier claims. It asserts nothing itself.
UsageHas epi:claimedBy and optionally epi:claimedAt. Disjoint with epi:Claim. A retracted claim is not admitted. Only claims can be retracted, not retractions.
ex:ret_form
  a epi:Retraction ;
  epi:claimedBy ex:src_form ;
  epi:claimedAt "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime ;
  epi:retracts ex:c_form_address .

epi:ScopedChain

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#ScopedChain
LabelScoped Chain
Subclass ofowl:Thing
DefinitionA chain of criteria that replaces the default chain for one property or one class.
UsageHas one epi:appliesTo and one epi:criteria. Claims in a conflict that fall under different scopes are compared with the default chain.
ex:chain_address
  a epi:ScopedChain ;
  epi:appliesTo ex:registeredAddress ;
  epi:criteria ( epi:ByRecency epi:ByTier ) .

epi:Source

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#Source
LabelSource
Subclass ofprov:Entity
DefinitionA document, registry, model or person that claims come from.
UsageCarries the trust: an epi:tier and an optional epi:admissionFloor. Corresponds to a HydraDL Source. A source with no tier is the least trusted in a comparison by tier.
ex:src_registry
  a epi:Source ;
  epi:tier 3 .

Named Individuals

Resolution criteria (epi:Criterion)

IndividualLabelDefinition
epi:ByConfidenceby confidencePrefer the claim with the higher confidence, if it leads by more than the margin.
epi:ByRecencyby recencyPrefer the claim claimed later.
epi:ByTierby tierPrefer the claim whose source has the higher tier.

Claim statuses (epi:ClaimStatus)

IndividualLabelDefinition
epi:AcceptedacceptedThe claim is in every optimal repair: it holds however the conflicts are resolved.
epi:ContestedcontestedThe claim is in some optimal repairs but not all: the policy cannot choose.
epi:NotAdmittednot admittedThe claim was left out before conflicts were considered: retracted, below the floor or superseded.
epi:RejectedrejectedThe claim is in no optimal repair: a preferred claim wins against it.
epi:UndeterminedundeterminedThe claim's group could not be settled: the reasoner answered unknown or a budget was exceeded.

Object Properties

PropertyDomainRangeCharacteristicsDefinition
epi:appliesToepi:ScopedChain—FunctionalPropertyThe property or class IRI whose claims a scoped chain governs.
A property IRI scopes claims whose predicate it is; a class IRI scopes claims that assert membership of the class. No range is declared because the value is a property or a class used as a value.
epi:assessesepi:Assessmentepi:ClaimFunctionalPropertyThe claim an assessment is about.
Exactly one claim per assessment.
epi:claimedBy——FunctionalProperty, ⊑ prov:wasAttributedToThe source that makes the claim or the retraction.
Points at an epi:Source in the executable profile. Nested attribution ("the broker reports that the insured said ...") points at an epi:Claim instead; the range is therefore left open and the profile shapes report the nesting as gap E1. A builder may align the property differently (for example with prov:wasAttributedTo directly).
epi:comparesepi:Decisionepi:Claim—One of the two claims a decision compared.
Every decision compares exactly two claims, whether a criterion decided the pair or not; it does not say which claim is preferred. When a criterion decided, the two are the decision's epi:winner and epi:loser.
epi:corroboratesepi:Claimepi:Claim—The claim agrees with another claim from an independent source.
Agreement between independent sources should raise belief (gap E2). The engine does not count agreement: it compares claims only when they conflict.
epi:criteriaepi:ResolutionPolicy or epi:ScopedChainrdf:ListFunctionalPropertyThe ordered list of epi:Criterion individuals tried in turn until one decides.
A pair no criterion decides is left undecided, and the claims stay contested: its epi:Decision names the two claims (epi:compares) but no epi:winner, epi:loser or epi:decidedBy.
epi:decidedByepi:Decisionepi:CriterionFunctionalPropertyThe criterion that decided the comparison.
Present exactly once, with epi:winner and epi:loser, when a criterion of the chain decided the pair; absent, with both of them, when none did.
epi:hasScopedChainepi:ResolutionPolicyepi:ScopedChain—A chain of criteria for one property or class that the policy uses.
Several scoped chains may be given, at most one per property or class.
epi:involvesepi:Conflictepi:Claim—A claim that takes part in a conflict.
A conflict involves one claim or more.
epi:loserepi:Decisionepi:ClaimFunctionalProperty, ⊑ epi:comparesThe claim a decision set aside.
Present only when a criterion decided the pair, together with epi:winner and epi:decidedBy; an undecided decision has no loser. The loser is the other of the two claims the decision epi:compares.
epi:retractsepi:Retractionepi:Claim—The claim the retraction withdraws.
A retraction may name several claims.
epi:statusepi:Assessmentepi:ClaimStatusFunctionalPropertyThe status an assessment gives its claim.
One of the five epi:ClaimStatus individuals.
epi:supersedesepi:Claimepi:Claim—The claim is a correction that replaces the claim it points at.
The replaced claim is not admitted (status not admitted) whatever its conflicts, unless its replacement is itself not admitted (retracted or below the floor). A superseding cycle is invalid; a claim that supersedes a retraction or an unknown claim is invalid.
epi:trustedForepi:Source——A topic or jurisdiction for which the source is trusted at its tier.
Contextual trust beyond the per-property and per-class scopes of a policy (gap E5). The engine does not run it.
epi:trustLevelepi:Sourceskos:Concept—A graded trust given as a concept of a trust scale instead of an integer tier.
Outside the executable profile (gap E6): the engine reads only epi:tier.
epi:winnerepi:Decisionepi:ClaimFunctionalProperty, ⊑ epi:comparesThe claim a decision preferred.
Present only when a criterion decided the pair, together with epi:loser and epi:decidedBy; an undecided decision has no winner. The winner is one of the two claims the decision epi:compares.

Datatype Properties

PropertyDomainRangeCharacteristicsDefinition
epi:admissionFloorepi:Source or epi:ResolutionPolicyxsd:decimalFunctionalPropertyThe lowest confidence, a decimal in [0, 1], at which a claim is admitted.
On a source it applies to that source's claims; on a policy it applies to every source without a floor of its own. A claim whose confidence is below the floor is not admitted. A claim with no confidence is not below any floor.
epi:claimedAt—xsd:dateTimeFunctionalPropertyThe instant at which the source made the claim or the retraction.
Used by the recency criterion. Value type xsd:dateTime, in UTC: the HydraDL engine reads whole seconds and does not support xsd:date. Not the time at which the claimed fact holds (see epi:validFrom).
epi:comparedValuesepi:Decisionxsd:stringFunctionalPropertyThe values the deciding criterion compared, in plain language.
The engine's wording is: tier A over tier B; confidence A over B (margin M); claimed at A, after B; or, for an undecided pair, "undecided after" and the criteria tried (undecided after tier, confidence, recency), with " (preference cycle)" appended when the pair was dropped from a cycle of preferences. A scoped chain appends " [chain for P]".
epi:confidenceepi:Claimxsd:decimalFunctionalPropertyHow sure the source is of the claim, a decimal in [0, 1].
Optional. An absent score means not stated, not 1.0: the epistemic layer does not invent a number, and a claim with no confidence is never below a floor and never decides a comparison by confidence. LDSO-Annotations reads an absent ann:confidence as 1.0 for human-curated annotations; the two properties are therefore related by skos:closeMatch and not declared equivalent. A claim derived from an ann:EntityMention copies its confidence when the mention states one and states none otherwise. The engine keeps six decimal places exactly.
epi:confidenceMarginepi:ResolutionPolicyxsd:decimalFunctionalPropertyHow far apart two confidences must be, in [0, 1], for confidence to decide.
A difference equal to the margin does not decide.
epi:negatedepi:Claimxsd:booleanFunctionalPropertyWhether the claim denies its triple. Absent: false.
A denied object or data property assertion is a negative property assertion in the engine. A denied rdf:type claim is the assertion of the complement class (ClassAssertion of ObjectComplementOf C); it is compared by the default chain, not by a scoped chain for C. A denied owl:sameAs claim is an owl:differentFrom claim (DifferentIndividuals) and a denied owl:differentFrom claim is an owl:sameAs claim (SameIndividual).
epi:reasonepi:Assessmentxsd:stringFunctionalPropertyThe plain-language reason for the status.
The engine's wording is: no conflict; retracted by R; confidence C below floor F; superseded by X; in conflict N, M; undetermined: message.
epi:tierepi:Sourcexsd:nonNegativeIntegerFunctionalPropertyThe trust rank of a source: a higher tier is more trusted.
Only the order matters. A tier that is not a non-negative integer (a SKOS trust scale, one source rating another) is gap E6; trust depending on topic or jurisdiction is gap E5.
epi:validFromepi:Claimxsd:dateTimeFunctionalPropertyThe instant from which the claimed fact holds.
Valid time of the fact, not the time of the claim (gap E3): with it, a change over time would not be a conflict. The engine ignores it.
epi:validUntilepi:Claimxsd:dateTimeFunctionalPropertyThe instant until which the claimed fact holds.
See epi:validFrom (gap E3).

SHACL Validation

shapes.ttl checks the structural well-formedness of any LDSO-Epistemic data. hydradl-profile-shapes.ttl restricts it to what the HydraDL epistemic engine executes. Validate data merged with its imported ontologies; see the RDF → Rust mapping section.

Competency Questions

Competency questions define what the module must be able to answer. Each question is stated in natural language and paired with a SPARQL query validated against the example named on its Against: line (tests/test_epistemic.py runs every query and requires a non-empty answer).

Questions about which claims win are not answered by SPARQL: they need the belief-revision engine (HydraDL, hydradl-epistemic), which decides against the trusted ontology. CQ-E-5 to CQ-E-7 read the stored result (Layer 6) that the engine produced; CQ-E-1 to CQ-E-4 read the inputs. A stored decision names a winner and a loser only when a criterion decided it (it then has an epi:decidedBy); every decision, decided or not, names its two claims with epi:compares.

This document is not an official W3C Standard or W3C Recommendation. It is a community/project specification using W3C ReSpec formatting conventions.

Prefixes used throughout:

PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX epi: <https://w3id.org/ldso/epistemic#>
PREFIX ex:  <https://example.org/kyc/>

Claims and sources

CQ-E-1 — Which claims did a given source make?

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

SELECT ?claim ?subject ?predicate ?object WHERE {
  ?claim a epi:Claim ;
         epi:claimedBy ex:newsA ;
         rdf:subject ?subject ;
         rdf:predicate ?predicate ;
         rdf:object ?object .
}
ORDER BY ?claim

Expected on kyc.ttl: four claims of ex:newsA: ex:nerDoi, ex:nerShell, ex:newsControl and ex:newsUk.

CQ-E-2 — Which claims correct another claim, and what do they correct?

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

SELECT ?correction ?corrected WHERE {
  ?correction epi:supersedes ?corrected .
}
ORDER BY ?correction

Expected on kyc.ttl: one row, ex:formAddrNew corrects ex:formAddrOld.

Resolution policy

CQ-E-3 — Which chain of criteria settles conflicts about registeredAddress, in order?

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

SELECT ?position ?criterion WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?criterion (COUNT(?before) AS ?position) WHERE {
      ?policy epi:hasScopedChain ?chain .
      ?chain epi:appliesTo ex:registeredAddress ;
             epi:criteria ?list .
      ?list rdf:rest* ?before .
      ?before rdf:rest* ?cell .
      ?cell rdf:first ?criterion .
    }
    GROUP BY ?criterion
  }
}
ORDER BY ?position

Expected on kyc.ttl: position 1 epi:ByRecency, position 2 epi:ByTier. A conflict about any other property uses the policy's default chain: epi:ByTier, epi:ByConfidence, epi:ByRecency.

CQ-E-4 — Which claims are below the admission floor, computed from their confidence?

The floor of a source applies to its own claims; otherwise the floor of the policy does. A claim with no confidence is never below a floor.

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

SELECT ?claim ?confidence ?floor WHERE {
  ?claim a epi:Claim ;
         epi:confidence ?confidence ;
         epi:claimedBy ?source .
  ?policy a epi:ResolutionPolicy ;
          epi:admissionFloor ?policyFloor .
  OPTIONAL { ?source epi:admissionFloor ?sourceFloor }
  BIND (COALESCE(?sourceFloor, ?policyFloor) AS ?floor)
  FILTER (?confidence < ?floor)
}
ORDER BY ?claim

Expected on kyc.ttl: one row, ex:nerShell (confidence 0.4, floor 0.5).

Results

CQ-E-5 — Which claims are contested, according to the stored assessment?

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

SELECT ?claim ?reason WHERE {
  ?assessment a epi:Assessment ;
              epi:assesses ?claim ;
              epi:status epi:Contested ;
              epi:reason ?reason .
}
ORDER BY ?claim

Expected on kyc.ttl: ex:newsCy and ex:newsUk, both in conflict 3: the policy cannot choose between them (same tier, confidences 0.91 and 0.88 within the margin, no claim time).

CQ-E-6 — Which decision rejected ex:newsControl, and by which criterion?

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

Only a decided pair has a loser; the query also requires the criterion.

SELECT ?decision ?winner ?criterion ?values WHERE {
  ?decision a epi:Decision ;
            epi:loser ex:newsControl ;
            epi:winner ?winner ;
            epi:decidedBy ?criterion ;
            epi:comparedValues ?values .
}
ORDER BY ?decision

Expected on kyc.ttl: two decisions, both by epi:ByTier: ex:formCleared over it ("tier 2 over tier 1") and ex:sancIvan over it ("tier 3 over tier 1"). The claim is rejected because the sanctioned person's claim outranks it as well.

CQ-E-7 — Which pairs of claims did no criterion decide, and what was tried?

An undecided decision has no epi:winner, epi:loser or epi:decidedBy; its two claims are read from epi:compares.

Against: examples/kyc.ttl

SELECT ?decision ?first ?second ?values WHERE {
  ?decision a epi:Decision ;
            epi:compares ?first , ?second ;
            epi:comparedValues ?values .
  FILTER (STR(?first) < STR(?second))
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?decision epi:decidedBy ?criterion }
}
ORDER BY ?decision

Expected on kyc.ttl: one row, ex:d_country comparing ex:newsCy and ex:newsUk ("undecided after tier, confidence, recency"), the decision behind their contested status (CQ-E-5).
